Physical/modelling defect inherited from the body of E260: friction is taken proportional to pressure, analogous to solid (Coulomb) friction. This is why the atmospheric height l enters. The 'loss' M = (3/400)Nn feet is then independent of flow velocity and is subtracted even at vanishing flow, so v can come out negative for small q. Real pipe head loss depends on velocity (roughly v² for turbulent flow) and not on ambient pressure. The rule is therefore only a rough empirical fit.

ideas.what: Head loss in a long conduit taken to depend only on the ratio of length to diameter n = L/D, with an experimentally fitted constant (g/α ≈ 4000 d)
ideas.modern_name: L/D scaling of pipe friction losses (as in Darcy–Weisbach h_f = f (L/D) V²/2g)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chézy (1775, via hydraulic radius); Weisbach (1845) and Darcy (1857) for the L/D form
ideas.where_published: E260 itself (Novi Comm. Petrop. 6); the friction theory is discussed by Truesdell in the Opera omnia II.12/13 introductions

ideas.what: Fountain jet height from reservoir head minus friction loss, reduced to a tabulable rule v = Nq − M
ideas.modern_name: Engineering head-loss computation for gravity-fed jets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mariotte (Traité du mouvement des eaux, 1686) and the later hydraulics tradition

ideas.what: Power-series expansion of (1 − e^{−x})/x for numerical tabulation
ideas.modern_name: Taylor series of the exponential relative (phi-function φ1)

missed.claim: Euler isolates L/D as the single dimensionless parameter governing friction loss in a pipe and proposes tabulating the loss against it. This is an early instance of the form later standard in Darcy–Weisbach, although his underlying pressure-proportional friction law is wrong. The priority point is mildly interesting, but histories of hydraulics (Rouse & Ince; Truesdell) do discuss Euler's friction memoir, so it is likely not wholly unknown.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historiographic interest for the prehistory of the Darcy–Weisbach equation. It has no modern mathematical consequence.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine application of E260's (physically flawed) pressure-proportional friction law to fountains, with correct series manipulation. The L/D scaling is a small historical curiosity but is not hidden.
